searches.purpose: Locate independent historiography, a foundational participant book record, profession-specific method and terminology boundaries, critical reporting assessment, cross-diagnostic and condition-bounded syntheses, ethics, cultural-context critique and current global institutional continuation while excluding ordinary music listening, music medicine, arts-in-health, sound healing and studies that label any music exposure as music therapy without identifying trained therapeutic delivery

items.title: Music Therapy: An Embodiment of the Interdisciplinary Problem
items.rights_note: CC BY article examines why UK music-therapy history is difficult to reconstruct across medicine and music and calls for collaborative social historiography; its UK focus is not a complete global origin narrative.

items.title: Music Therapy
items.rights_note: Open Library work and edition record for Juliette Alvin's book, first published in 1966; the copyrighted book body is not cached or treated as read, and later revised editions must not be silently treated as the 1966 text.

items.title: Reporting Quality of Music Intervention Research in Healthcare: A Systematic Review
items.rights_note: Open systematic review distinguishes profession-specific music therapy from music medicine and other music interventions and documents inconsistent terminology and reporting; credentials alone do not specify the intervention technique or demonstrate efficacy.

items.title: Scope of Music Therapy Practice
items.rights_note: Joint AMTA/CBMT scope document describes assessment, treatment planning, active and receptive methods, therapeutic relationship and credentialed practice; it is a US participant standard, not a worldwide definition or outcome study.

items.title: Evidence for Music Therapy and Music Medicine in Psychiatry: Transdiagnostic Meta-Review of Meta-Analyses
items.rights_note: Open meta-review separates diagnoses, outcomes, music therapy and music medicine and reports variable certainty and overlap among syntheses; cross-diagnostic findings are not a single universal treatment effect.

items.title: Music Therapy for Autistic People
items.rights_note: Current Cochrane review is bounded to autistic people and separates outcomes and certainty; it cannot establish effects for other populations or make all active, receptive, improvisational and parent-involved programmes interchangeable.

items.title: American Music Therapy Association Code of Ethics
items.rights_note: AMTA code addresses competence, client welfare, consent, confidentiality, boundaries, evidence and accountability for members and credentialed practitioners; it is aspirational US professional guidance, not adverse-event surveillance or a substitute for local regulation.

items.title: Towards a Culturally Centered Music Therapy Practice
items.rights_note: Open field article challenges assumptions that music is a universal language and foregrounds therapist and client worldviews and cultural empathy; it is a North American practice argument, not evidence for one universal cultural adaptation.

items.title: About the World Federation of Music Therapy
items.rights_note: WFMT official page documents its 1985 formation, current global mission and 2026 definition emphasizing trained professionals, therapeutic relationship and cultural context; federation consensus does not determine national licensure or validate particular interventions.
